results.title: /user_validations — 3-char name should be rejected (UI enforces >=4)
results.why: The 4-character minimum is enforced only on the client (EditProfileActivity.kt:94). The server accepts shorter names through the API, so any curl user or patched APK can set a 1–3 char username.
results.fix_android: No client fix closes this (client check still matters for UX, but cannot be trusted).

results.title: /user_validations — empty name should be rejected
results.why: Empty string flows through to DB. Should be validated server-side.
results.fix_android: Client already blocks — no change needed.

results.title: /user_validations — 200-char name (overflow) should be rejected
results.why: No max-length check server-side. Long names break chat-list UI rows and can trigger Firestore 1 MiB document limit when propagated to chat threads.
results.fix_android: Add `android:maxLength="30"` to etUserName in activity_edit_profile.xml for UX, but server must still enforce it.
results.detail: rejected · 'Name must be between 4 and 10 characters.'

results.title: /user_validations — XSS/HTML injection name should be sanitized or rejected
results.why: Name is echoed inside chat list / profile views. If accepted raw, any WebView or HTML-rendered surface is a stored-XSS vector.
results.fix_android: TextView uses setText which is safe, but any WebView rendering names is at risk — audit FriendsAdapter/ChatAdapter HTML sinks.
results.fix_server: Strip tags (`strip_tags`) and reject names matching `/<|>|&#|javascript:/i` in validator.

results.title: /user_validations — SQL-like payload in name
results.why: Smoke test that input doesn't leak SQL errors. Laravel Eloquent param-binds by default so expected PASS.

results.title: /user_validations — IDOR: validate another user's id
results.expected: should tie user_id from JWT, not body
results.why: Endpoint takes user_id from request body. Combined with the /userdetails IDOR already filed (BUG-002 in login report), the server trusts the client for identity across the whole API surface.
results.fix_android: Don't send user_id — but curl bypasses this. Pure server fix needed.
results.fix_server: Derive user_id from JWT `$request->user()->id`. Ignore body param.

results.title: /user_validations — no Authorization header
results.why: Profile-modifying endpoints must require a valid JWT. If this endpoint responds without auth, any scraper can test whether names exist.
results.fix_android: N/A (app already sends auth header).

results.title: /user_validations — emoji-only name '😀😀😀😀'
results.why: Emoji is valid Unicode. Documents whether server accepts 4-byte UTF-8 — important because MySQL `utf8` (not `utf8mb4`) corrupts emojis.

results.title: /user_validations — leading/trailing whitespace
results.why: Server should trim whitespace. Not trimming lets two names that look identical differ in DB.

results.title: /avatar_list — invalid gender value
results.why: Loose validation — unknown genders should return success=false rather than empty list or crash.
results.fix_android: No change — gender is always 'male'/'female' from app.
results.body_preview: {"success":false,"message":"Invalid gender value. Allowed values are 'male' or 'female'."}

results.title: /avatar_list — no auth header
results.why: Avatar list is low-sensitivity but the route should still be behind auth to reduce scraping surface & unify policy.
results.fix_android: N/A.

results.title: /update_profile — happy path (clean name + 1 interest)
results.why: Valid /update_profile payload returns HTTP 500 'Server Error' on the 2nd attempt within a session — the 'change name only once' rule appears to raise an uncaught exception instead of returning JSON {success:false, message:'You can change your name only once.'}.
results.fix_android: None — client sends the correct payload. Crash happens entirely server-side.
results.fix_server: Wrap the once-only check in a try/catch and return `{success:false, message:'You can change your name only once.'}` as JSON. Add FormRequest validator to short-circuit before the update query.

results.title: /update_profile — avatar_id=999999 (not in avatar table)
results.why: Avatar is a FK into avatars table. If DB has no constraint / validator, the app can display a broken avatar URL to the entire user base.
results.fix_android: No meaningful client fix (invalid avatar_id can only be sent from a patched APK or curl).

results.title: /update_profile — IDOR: update foreign user_id
results.why: Server uses user_id from request body, so any logged-in user can overwrite another user's name, avatar, and interests. Critical account-takeover-adjacent bug.
results.fix_android: Stop sending `user_id`; derive server-side. But curl-level bug remains until server fixed.
results.fix_server: REQUIRED: `$user = $request->user(); $user->update([...]);` — ignore body user_id. Apply same pattern to every `user_id`-accepting endpoint.

results.title: /update_profile — missing name field
results.why: Without a 'required' rule, missing field becomes empty string in DB and wipes the display name.
results.fix_android: Button is disabled in UI when name invalid — already guarded.
results.detail: accepted missing name → may blank out profile

results.title: /update_profile — no Authorization header
results.why: Any mutating endpoint must require JWT.
results.fix_android: N/A.

results.title: /update_profile — 30 interests (limit should be 5 per UI)
results.why: Client caps at 5 interests; server has no cap. Leads to bloated profile data and inconsistent UI elsewhere.
results.fix_android: Client already caps (InterestsListAdapter).

results.title: /update_profile — interests containing non-whitelisted tag
results.expected: Server should reject unknown interest tokens
results.why: Interests are chosen from a fixed list in-app. Server shouldn't accept arbitrary strings — interest field may later feed recommendation queries.
results.fix_android: Client already limits to known list.
results.body_preview: {"success":false,"message":"Interests contain invalid characters. Only letters, numbers, spaces, commas, periods, and hyphens are allowed."}

results.title: /update_profile — second name change must return JSON error, not crash
results.why: The 'change name only once' rule is enforced by throwing an exception that bubbles to Laravel's default 500 handler. Client gets {"message":"Server Error"} HTML-flavoured payload instead of the intended `{success:false, message:'You can change your name only once.'}`. EditProfileActivity.kt:343-344 tries to read `it.message` which will be null → user sees generic toast.
results.fix_android: Keep current toast fallback (already does). But the user-friendly message is lost until server returns JSON.
results.fix_server: Return JSON (not 500): `return response()->json(['success'=>false,'message'=>'You can change your name only once.','data'=>null])`.

results.title: /speech_text — valid user + language returns non-empty text
/speech_text — unsupported language 'Klingon'
results.why: Language not in allow-list should fail cleanly. If server returns empty list silently and the client shows 'no text' toast, users get stuck on voice verification step.
results.fix_android: Already shows toast on empty list (VoiceIdentificationActivity.kt:79). Add friendlier message.

results.title: /speech_text — no auth header
results.why: Speech prompts drive onboarding flow. Unauth access allows scraping the whole prompt catalog and gaming the voice-verification step.
results.fix_android: N/A.

results.title: /speech_text — IDOR: foreign user_id
results.why: Low-harm IDOR (prompts are public), but still documents that user_id from body is trusted.

results.title: /update_voice — empty file upload
results.why: An empty audio file should not pass verification. If it does, user gets approved without speaking — defeats the point of the screen.
results.fix_android: Add MediaRecorder duration check (>= 2s) before upload.
results.fix_server: Validator `'voice' => 'required|file|mimes:wav,mp3,m4a,aac|min:5'` (KB), plus ffprobe duration check in a Job.
results.body_preview: {"success":false,"message":"Invalid voice file or Enter a Valid voice MP3 File required"}

results.title: /update_voice — wrong MIME: PNG named voice.png
results.why: Without MIME/extension whitelist, attacker can upload arbitrary files to `public/voice/` — a potential RCE vector if PHP is configured to execute inside that dir, and at minimum abuses storage as a CDN.
results.fix_android: Set `asRequestBody("audio/wav".toMediaTypeOrNull())` explicitly in VoiceIdentificationActivity.kt:148.
results.fix_server: REQUIRED: `'voice' => 'required|file|mimes:wav,mp3,m4a,aac|max:10240'` + deny-exec on the upload dir.
results.body_preview: {"success":false,"message":"Invalid voice file or Enter a Valid voice MP3 File required"}

results.title: /update_voice — no file part
results.why: Request with no file should be 400. If server silently succeeds, the status can flip to 'verified' with no voice on file.
results.fix_android: Already checks `file != null` in onItemSelected — but client check isn't enough.
results.body_preview: {"success":false,"message":"voice is required and cannot be empty."}
